task_description: You extract structured data from the OCR text of an invoice. Return one JSON object with exactly these keys: invoice_number, date, due_date, vendor_name, vendor_address, bill_to_name, bill_to_address, po_number, payment_terms, currency, subtotal, tax_rate, tax_amount, total_amount, line_items. Dates are ISO YYYY-MM-DD whatever format the invoice uses. currency is the ISO 4217 code (e.g. USD, GBP, EUR, INR, AUD, CAD). Money amounts are strings copied as printed without the currency symbol (e.g. "3,567.71"). tax_rate is a number in percent (10.0 for 10%). line_items is a list of {description, quantity (integer), unit_price (string), total (string)}; do not include freight or tax as line items unless the invoice lists them as items. Use null for a field the invoice does not show. Output JSON only. bill_to_address is the street address only, never the 'Attn:' contact line. Numeric slash dates are MM/DD for US vendors and DD/MM for all other vendors.
llm_as_a_judge_instructions: Compare the predicted JSON with the reference field by field. Count each of the 14 top-level fields and the line_items list (all items match in order) as one criterion: 15 criteria. A field matches when the values are equal after ignoring case, whitespace and thousands separators. Output the fraction of criteria that match as a number between 0 and 1 inside the score tag, for example <score>0.93</score>.
synthetic_data_generation_instructions: Each input is the OCR-style plain text of a business invoice that keeps the printed layout: a title line (INVOICE, Invoice, TAX INVOICE or COMMERCIAL INVOICE, sometimes on the same line as the vendor name), the vendor name and one-line address, a key: value header block (invoice number, issue date, due date, optional PO number, terms), a bill-to block with its own label (Bill To, Billed To, Sold To, Customer), the customer name, an Attn: contact line and a one-line address (the Attn contact is never part of bill_to_address in the answer), a line-item table with aligned columns (Description, Qty, Unit Price, Amount), and a totals block (Subtotal, one tax line with its rate, and a final total labelled Total, Grand Total, Total Due, Amount Due or Balance Due). Vary layouts (classic, modern, compact, two-column header, ledger), the vendor country (US, UK, IN, AU, FR, CA, DE) and the bill-to country independently, 1-12 line items (repeated descriptions with different prices are allowed), optional PO numbers (about 40% of invoices have none), terms (Net 15/30/45/60, Due on receipt). The currency follows the vendor's country and its symbol is printed on the totals: $ for US (USD), A$ for AU (AUD), CA$ for CA (CAD), £ for UK (GBP), € for FR and DE (EUR), ₹ for IN (INR, Indian digit grouping is not used: 1,234,567.89). Tax lines match the country: Sales Tax (x%) for US, VAT for UK/FR/DE, GST for IN/AU, GST/HST for CA. Dates appear in many printed forms (2025-03-27, 27 Mar 2025, Mar 27, 2025, March 27, 2025, numeric slash dates). Numeric slash dates are MM/DD/YYYY only for US vendors and DD/MM/YYYY for every other vendor country; the answer converts them accordingly to YYYY-MM-DD. Totals must add up: each line amount = qty x unit price, subtotal = sum of line amounts, tax = subtotal x rate rounded to cents, total = subtotal + tax. In the answer, money amounts are copied exactly as printed without the symbol, keeping thousands separators; fields not printed are null.
